cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: Tenth concept, and the most native-feeling in the set. One-to-one replication of the GLP-1 SOS whiteboard ad (TrendTrack share glp-1-sos-supplements-y9N6mT), fourth creative ported from this direct competitor. A real phone photo of a physical dry-erase board propped on a granite kitchen counter, everything hand-drawn in marker, a vertical split with a hand-lettered heading and a hand-drawn torso on each side, hand-lettered payoff across the bottom, real jar leaning on the counter. Their headings named Wegovy; ours name no drug at all. Three payoff variations, identical board. 9:16 at 1080x1920, all three cleared on the first roll.

cards.title: OURS · three payoffs, one board  ·  ours

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: WHY THIS FORMAT IS THE STRONGEST IN THE SET
cards.text:
Everything else we have built looks like an ad. THIS ONE LOOKS LIKE A PHOTOGRAPH SOMEONE TOOK OF A THING THEY MADE.

That is the entire mechanism. The wobbly marker lines, the ghosting from previous erasing, the kitchen jars out of focus behind it, the bottle just leaning on the counter. It reads as a person explaining something they figured out, not a brand making a claim. On a feed full of polished supplement graphics, a handmade whiteboard is the pattern interrupt.

It also carries more mechanism than any other creative here without a single sentence of body copy.

cards.title: THE TWO DRAWINGS
cards.text:
Both torsos are the same size, drawn in the same hand, so the comparison is between the INSIDES rather than the bodies.

LEFT, under ON A GLP-1: stomach full and heavy in murky olive-brown. Large intestine loops thick, swollen and congested, dull greyish olive. Small hand-drawn circles floating all around the abdomen as trapped gas. Belly outline bulging.

RIGHT, under GLP-1 + MOTILLI: stomach light and mostly empty with pale shading. Intestine loops neat, even, normal width, healthy warm pink. No floating circles anywhere. Belly outline flat.

THE GAS CIRCLES ARE DOING QUIET WORK. They are the only element that appears on one side and is completely absent on the other, so the eye finds the difference before it reads a word.

cards.title: WHAT WE CHANGED FROM THE REFERENCE
cards.text:
THEIR HEADINGS NAME WEGOVY. OURS NAME NO DRUG.
'ON WEGOVY' / 'WEGOVY + GLP-1 SOS' becomes 'ON A GLP-1' / 'GLP-1 + MOTILLI'.

Two reasons. Naming a specific branded drug on-creative invites a trademark problem their own body copy has to disclaim away with Novo and Lilly lines, and none of our other nine concepts name one. And 'a GLP-1' addresses everyone on semaglutide or tirzepatide rather than one brand's users, which is a bigger audience for the same creative.

THEIR PAYOFF LINE IS THEIRS. 'Lose weight, not your gut health.' is a good line and it stays with them. All three of ours are written fresh.

THEIR BOTTLE was never passed as a reference image. Our jar is the only product input.

cards.title: PRODUCTION NOTE · making it read as a real photo
cards.text:
Name the physical evidence. Wobbly amateur marker lines, uneven hand-lettering, visible marker texture, faint smudges and ghosting on the board from previous erasing, blurred kitchen shelves behind, granite speckle, slight sensor noise, handheld feel.

Asking for 'whiteboard illustration' produces a clean vector. The imperfections are the instruction.

THE JAR OVERLAPS the bottom lettering slightly in H1 and H3. The reference does the same thing so it reads as authentic rather than broken, but H2 is the one where the whole board is clear if you want a hero.

cards.title: SHARED PRIMARY TEXT
cards.text:
Somebody drew this on a whiteboard in their kitchen, and it explains the whole thing better than the pamphlet did.

On the left is what a GLP-1 does to your gut when nothing else changes. The medication slows digestion down on purpose, because that is how it quiets your appetite, and it works. But the slowdown does not stop at your stomach. It reaches all the way to your colon.

Your colon is a muscle, and it only contracts when something tells it to. That signal is a short-chain fatty acid called butyrate, and you do not make it yourself. The bacteria in your colon make it out of the fiber that reaches them. Slow everything down, less reaches them, the colony thins out, and the signal fades. What stays behind sits there and ferments, which is where the gas and the afternoon distension come from.

On the right is the same gut with the signal restored. Concentrated celery juice standardized for a real dose of apigenin, which barely absorbs into your bloodstream and so stays down in the colon where the problem actually is, calming the lining and shifting the balance back toward the bacteria that matter. Plus a fine soluble prebiotic fiber to feed those bacteria once they come back.

Rebuild the place, then feed what grows there. Nothing is forced, so there is no cramping and no urgency.

The important part is that these are two separate systems. Weight loss lives in the brain and the appetite, which is the dial the medication turns. This lives in the colon. You can rebuild one and stay on the other. Nobody has to choose.

Two gummies before bed with a full glass of water. Sixty in a bottle. Third-party tested, lab results posted. Not a laxative, so the first few days are quiet and it fills in over the following weeks.

Ninety days to decide. Email inside ninety days and every dollar comes back, no return required.

cards.title: FRAME QA · all three
cards.text:
Headings: PASS. ON A GLP-1 left, GLP-1 + MOTILLI right, hand-lettered, GLP-1 hyphenated correctly in both. No drug brand name anywhere.

Drawings: PASS. Two torsos, same size, same hand. Left congested olive with gas circles and bulging belly. Right neat pink with no circles and flat belly. Difference obvious at a glance.

Payoff: PASS. Hand-lettered, spelled exactly, plus 'Try Motilli risk-free.' beneath in all three.

Board: PASS. Physical dry-erase board in a black frame, propped on granite, blurred kitchen shelves behind, marker ghosting present.

Jar: PASS. Real photographed jar on the counter leaning against the board, motilli wordmark and CELERY JUICE FIBER GUMMIES legible.

No invented words, badges, prices, star ratings or percentages.

cards.title: AUDIT
cards.text:
Law 2: no invented study, percentage, doctor, review count or customer quote.

Law 6: competitor intelligence stayed a brief direction. No line of their copy appears in ours, no comparison is drawn, and no competitor is named or alluded to.

Law 9: no em dashes, no negation-affirmation beats, no parallel stacks, no rhetorical openers.

Two separate systems: this concept IS the two-systems argument, drawn.

Swap test: PASS. The right-hand drawing shows a RESTORED colon rather than an emptied one, which is our mechanism and not a laxative's.

Shelf life: evergreen.

CLAIM RISK: low to moderate. No photographic body imagery, no before-and-after of a person. The drawing is clearly a hand illustration, which reads as explanation rather than evidence. Naming no drug brand removes the trademark exposure the reference carries.

VERIFY BEFORE LAUNCH: the 90-day no-return-required guarantee wording against the live policy page.
